quick.topic: After a record week, expect a step back
quick.summary: Why a change made after a record week can look like it failed.
quick.takeaway: An extreme week is usually followed by a more normal one.

parts.title: After a record week, expect a step back

beats.line: Record week, then we changed the homepage. This week fell. Did we break it?
Maybe not. What made last week a record?
Nothing special that we know of. It just went well.
Then this week was likely to fall anyway. Lucky weeks rarely repeat.

board.text: record week → next week nearer normal

beats.line: The textbook name is regression to the mean.
But what if the new homepage really did hurt?
It might. If this week is below your normal weeks, look closer.
So compare with normal weeks, not with the record.
This week matches our normal weeks. No sign the homepage broke anything.
Right. Judge it against normal, not against the best.

quiz.question: Sales fall the week after a record week, right after a change. What should you compare this week with?
options: A typical week before the record
The average of the record week and this week
quiz.explanation: After an unusual week, numbers usually move back toward normal, so the fair comparison is a typical week.

quiz.question: After an unusually good week, the following week is likely to be closer to normal, even if nothing changed.
quiz.explanation: Extreme results are partly luck, and luck does not usually repeat, so the next result drifts back.
